I stopped my friend from committing suicide.

We worked at the same place but really didn't work together so we had a basic friendship. One day he offered me a ride home (I used to walk, it wasn't a big deal for me). I was hesitant but something to me to say yes. We ended up going out for lunch/dinner and had a great time. During our dinner I noticed he sent a quick text message. The next day he told me that the message he sent was to his brother telling him to flush down the sleeping meds he had. He said that he had planned on killing himself that day after work.

I was having an end of term party with friends and cooking steak. The steak accidentally set off the fire alarm because we were in small dorm apartments and the fire alarm blared for 15 minutes before "help" came to turn it off. Not 10 minutes after they left my best friend started choking on a piece of my rare steak and motioned for the Heimlich maneuver. It was my first time ever performing it so I went easy the first time. Nothing came out. The second time I pulled as hard as I can and steak flew across the room. He said that when it failed the first time he thought to himself, "This is how I die. I can't even eat properly - the most basic human function." He would've been screwed if we had to rely on "help" that would've taken 15 more minutes. So I guess I'm both the one who almost killed him (the cook) and the savior.

Asura's Wrath. The combat can get a little repetitive at times but the set pieces and visuals are absolutely insane and the voice acting is nailed perfectly. If you love those ridiculous, over-the-top action scenes from shows like Dragon Ball Z, you'll love this game.

For example (SPOILERS) the first true boss fight in the game has you battle a skyscraper-tall fat god. You launch bursts of energy at each other before you punch him into space. Then the god transforms to be several times larger than the Earth and tries to squish you with a finger. You stop his finger and use your six arms to punch it basically at the speed of light, which sends a shockwave through the god's body and disintegrates him.

In another instance you punch another god all the way to the moon and fight him there. He has a sword that can infinitely grow. He gets you in the air, stabs at you with his sword, and you block it by grabbing the blade between your hands. He then extends his blade, pushing you all the way back to Earth. You land, creating a crater, and the sword starts going through your body. The god then jumps off the moon and flies toward you, still pushing the sword. You grab it with six arms to try to stop it, but four of your arms break away from the effort. The sword pierces all the way through the Earth, emerging on the other side. As the god is about to hit you with the hilt, you punch the blade, breaking both it and your arm. You then get up, grab the sword with your teeth, and slice him in half with it.

Seriously, if that at all interests you, get it. There's much more awesomeness to be had. Besides awesome set pieces, the setting and story are insanely original.
